abstract: Teratomas, the most common extragonadal germ cell tumor of childhood, involve at least two of the ectodermal, mesodermal, and endodermal layers. Of the teratomas seen in the first 2 months of life, 82% are sacrococcygeal. The head and neck region is the second most common location for teratomas in early infancy, accounting for five (14%) of those cases. We describe a female neonate with a teratoma of the nasopharyngeal area, bilateral cleft palate/lip, and columellar sinus pathologies. The mass, which was 8 x 5 x 7 cm and soft in consistency, blocked the airway and prevented oral feeding. On macroscopic examination of the excised mass, there was a notable typical cilia arrangement and lower eyelid appearance. The patient, who was diagnosed with a well-differentiated teratoma after the pathologic examination, did not have any complications in the postoperative period.
abstract_ja: 奇形腫は、小児において最も多い性腺外胚細胞腫瘍であり、外胚葉・中胚葉・内胚葉のうち少なくとも2層を含む。生後2か月以内に見つかる奇形腫の82％は仙尾部に生じる。乳児早期において頭頸部は奇形腫の第2の好発部位であり、そのうち5例（14％）を占める。われわれは、鼻咽頭部の奇形腫、両側口蓋裂・口唇裂、鼻柱洞の異常を伴う女児新生児を報告する。8×5×7cmの軟らかい腫瘤が気道を閉塞し、経口哺乳を妨げていた。切除した腫瘤の肉眼的検査では、典型的な線毛の配列と下眼瞼様の構造が認められた。病理検査で高分化型奇形腫と診断され、術後に合併症は認められなかった。
